caption: What if the Sun were a football? Shrink it to a 22 cm football and scale everything else the same way. Earth becomes a mustard seed about 2 mm wide, sitting about 24 metres away, just past the far end of a 20-metre cricket pitch. The Moon is a speck of sand 6 cm from that seed, and the ISS orbits barely a hair's width (about 0.06 mm) above it. Jupiter is a 2 cm marble about 123 metres out, past the boundary. Neptune is an 8 mm bead roughly 710 metres away. Big news: on 18 November 2026, NASA's Voyager 1 reached one light-day from Earth, about 25.9 billion km, after 49 years of flying. On our model that's only about 4 km. Plot twist: the nearest star, Proxima Centauri, would be about 6,300 km away, almost the distance from Delhi to London. Space is mostly empty space. Did YOU guess it was that far? 👇
